question: What is the primary aim of dietary counselling in nursing?

options.A: Strictly enforcing hospital meal schedules at home
options.B: Helping patients make informed food choices for better health
options.C: Prescribing expensive nutritional supplements for rapid weight loss
options.D: Diagnosing rare metabolic disorders without lab tests

explanation: Dietary counselling focuses on guiding individuals toward healthy food selections that suit their lifestyle and health needs. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h1)

question: Why must nurses consider local food availability during dietary counselling in Nigeria?

options.A: Patients are more likely to follow recommendations using accessible foods
options.B: Imported foods are always chemically unsafe for consumption
options.C: Hospital policies forbid mentioning foreign food items
options.D: Traditional foods have zero nutritional value

explanation: Practical dietary plans rely on foods that patients can easily buy and prepare within their local environment. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h1)

question: Measuring a patient's height and weight belongs to which assessment category?
explanation: Anthropometric measurements involve physical body dimensions like height, weight, and circumferences. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h2)

question: What does a 24-hour dietary recall primarily help the nurse discover?

options.A: Long-term vitamin storage in liver tissues
options.B: Future genetic predispositions to chronic diseases
options.D: The exact types and amounts of food eaten recently

explanation: A 24-hour recall captures a detailed picture of what the patient consumed over the past day. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h2)

question: What do the letters in the SMART goal acronym stand for?
explanation: SMART is a standard framework used to ensure goals are clear and attainable. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h3)

question: A hypertensive patient sets a goal to reduce salt intake. Which statement makes this a SMART goal?

options.A: I will eat food without any flavor to lower my blood pressure
options.B: I will stop eating all seasoned foods forever starting today
options.C: I will try to think about using less salt sometime next month
options.D: I will use half a teaspoon of salt or less per day starting tomorrow

explanation: This option provides a specific, measurable limit with a clear timeframe, fitting the SMART criteria. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h3)

question: Why must a dietary plan accommodate family meal sharing?

options.A: Isolation during meals reduces adherence to the prescribed diet
options.B: Shared meals always contain excessive calories
options.C: Cooking separate meals is required by hospital accreditation
options.D: Family members must eat the exact same medical diet

explanation: Patients are more likely to stick to a diet when it integrates smoothly with family eating patterns rather than isolating them. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h4)

question: Which factor is LEAST important when designing a personalized dietary plan?
explanation: Dietary counselling centers entirely on the patient's needs and context, not the personal preferences of the nurse. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h4)

question: What type of questioning encourages a patient to share detailed thoughts during counselling?
explanation: Open-ended questions allow patients to elaborate rather than giving simple yes or no answers. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of motivational interviewing in dietary counselling?

options.A: Explaining complex biochemical pathways of digestion
options.B: Helping patients discover their own internal reasons for change
options.D: Forcing immediate compliance through strict warnings

explanation: Motivational interviewing resolves ambivalence by guiding patients to voice their own motivations for healthier habits. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical barrier to dietary change?

options.A: Having unlimited financial resources for food
options.B: Lack of basic cooking skills or equipment
options.C: High cost of recommended healthy food items
options.D: Unsupportive family members sharing the household

explanation: Financial abundance facilitates food access rather than acting as a barrier to dietary modification. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h6)

question: A patient claims healthy food is too expensive in the local market. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Explore budget-friendly, nutrient-dense local food alternatives together
options.B: Advise the patient to skip meals to save money on groceries
options.C: Tell the patient to spend less money on non-essential clothing
options.D: Insist that health has no price and they must find the money

explanation: Problem-solving financial hurdles involves finding affordable, accessible local substitutes that fit the budget. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h6)

question: What does the teach-back method involve during patient education?

options.A: Asking the patient to repeat instructions in their own words
options.B: Giving the patient a written quiz graded by the physician
options.C: Having the nurse read the textbook chapter out loud
options.D: Asking family members to test the patient at home

explanation: Teach-back checks comprehension by having patients explain what they heard and plan to do. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h7)

question: Why do nurses use household objects like a fist to demonstrate portion sizes?

options.A: Patients are required to carry measuring cups everywhere
options.B: Hospital scales are too inaccurate for measuring food
options.C: Standard kitchen tools are illegal in clinical practice
options.D: It makes abstract measurements concrete and easy to visualize

explanation: Visual comparisons help patients estimate correct portions without needing specialized measuring equipment. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of follow-up visits in dietary counselling?

options.A: Conducting expensive laboratory tests every single day
options.B: Tracking progress and revising the plan when needed
options.C: Discharging the patient from all future healthcare registries
options.D: Punishing patients who failed to follow their diet

explanation: Follow-ups allow nurses to evaluate goal attainment and make necessary adjustments to the dietary strategy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h8)

question: How should a nurse respond when a patient fails to meet dietary goals?

options.A: Ignore the failure and pretend the goals were met
options.B: Discontinue counselling because the patient is non-compliant
options.C: Scold the patient to ensure strict obedience next time
options.D: Reassess barriers and modify the plan collaboratively

explanation: Unmet goals signal a need to troubleshoot obstacles and adjust the approach rather than assigning blame. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h8)
